info.description: Peer-to-peer home EV charger sharing. Authentication routes under /auth/* are served by Better Auth and are not listed here. Errors are application/problem+json.

post.description: Schedules the account for deletion in 7 days and signs it out on every device at once. Until then it cannot be signed in to; the emailed link undoes the request (POST /me/delete/cancel). After that, personal data is removed; past bookings and payments are kept without it, for accounting. Refused (409, with reasons) while a booking is not finished or a payment is still owed.

Keeps an account scheduled for deletion, using the token from the link in the deletion email. Works until the deletion falls due; then sign in again as usual. Needs no session: the deletion request signed every device out.

token.description: The token from the undo link in the deletion email

get.summary: Search bookable chargers near a point for a window
get.description: Online chargers accepting bookings, with an availability window covering the whole slot and no booking overlapping it, nearest first. Positions are approximate.
Listing, host summary, rating and free slots for the next 7 days. The address and exact position are included only for a driver with a confirmed, arrived or active booking at this charger.

post.description: Creates the host profile (once) and a Stripe Express account for payouts, and returns a fresh link to Stripe's onboarding.

country.description: Country of the host's payouts account, fixed when it is created. Listings are priced in its currency: EUR for IE, GBP for GB

post.description: Checks the charger can connect (Zappi v2.1, serial starting with 2, or Zappi GLO) and returns the OCPP URL, ChargeboxID and password to enter in the charger's account. The password is shown once and stored only as an argon2 hash. Asking again for a charger still connecting replaces its password.

location.description: Exact position; shown to drivers only once booked

get.summary: Wait for a charger to connect
get.description: Long-polls until the charger sends its first BootNotification, or `wait` seconds pass (capped by the server), then returns its state. Poll again while `connected` is false.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for the charger to connect (capped by the server)

patch.summary: Set a charger's price, availability and listing
patch.description: Changes only the fields sent. `availability` replaces every window; price, kWh cap and instant book apply to every window. Publishing (`acceptingBookings: true`) needs the charger online on firmware 5.794 or later, payouts enabled, tax details given and at least one window, otherwise 409 lists what is missing.

get.description: This month's earnings, sessions and kWh, an 8-week weekly series, a card per charger (status pill, listing switch, next booking), tonight's bookings and requests waiting for an answer. Periods are in the host's time zone and a booking counts in the period its slot starts in. Each booking is paid upfront as a destination charge to the host's account: a period shows what drivers paid (less refunds), the card fees passed on to the host, and what the host keeps, in the currency the host is paid in.
Every day from `from` to `to` (inclusive, at most 31 days; by default the next 30 days from today) with the bookings starting on it, in the host's time zone. Cancelled bookings are left out.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day, inclusive; defaults to 29 days after `from`

post.summary: Register a device for push notifications
post.description: iOS and Android send their FCM registration token; the web app sends its push subscription. A token already registered (by this account or another signed in on the same device) is moved to the caller and refreshed: 201 when new, 200 when known. Each account keeps its 10 most recently seen devices.

token.description: The FCM registration token (iOS devices register through FCM too)

endpoint.description: On a browser push service: fcm.googleapis.com, updates.push.services.mozilla.com, *.notify.windows.com or *.push.apple.com

subscription.description: The browser's PushSubscription, as `subscription.toJSON()` gives it

delete.summary: Stop push notifications to a device
delete.description: Call on sign-out. Another account's device is 404.

get.description: Every switch is on until the user turns it off.

patch.description: Changes only the switches sent; answers all of them.

post.description: Books a charger for a slot inside one of its availability windows; the slot is the charging window. The price is the slot's minutes at the hourly price, with no fee added, and is paid upfront: with instant book the booking is confirmed and the card charged at once; otherwise the price is held on the card until the host approves (charged) or declines or lets the request expire after 24 hours (released). A driver may have at most 3 requests waiting, and make a limited number of bookings an hour (429). An overlapping slot is 409 and nothing is charged; a declined card is 402. When the payment provider does not answer, the booking is returned with its payment `pending` and finished in the background.

from.description: Start of the slot, on a whole minute

to.description: End of the slot (exclusive), on a whole minute

vehiclePlate.description: Number plate of the car being charged; shown to the host

paymentMethodId.description: A saved card; the default card when omitted

get.description: Latest slot first; filter by status and by a window the slot overlaps.
For its driver or the host of its charger; anyone else gets 404. The driver sees the address and exact position only while the booking is confirmed, arrived or active.

post.description: The host of the charger confirms a requested booking; its idTag is issued and the price held on the driver's card is charged. 409 if the slot has been taken since or the hold is not in place yet; 402 when the hold has lapsed, which cancels the booking.
The host turns a request down; the hold on the driver's card is released.

The driver or the host cancels a requested or confirmed booking. A request's hold is released. A confirmed booking is refunded in full when the host cancels or the driver cancels before the host's cutoff (default 2 hours before the start), and not at all when the driver cancels after it. Once the driver has arrived a booking can only be stopped (409).

The driver says they have arrived, from a few hours before the slot starts (ARRIVAL_LEAD_MINUTES, 4 hours by default) until it ends: a confirmed, paid booking becomes arrived and the window-end stop is scheduled. 409 `payment-pending` while the payment has not gone through. A position (lat and lng), when sent, is compared with the charger's; the distance is recorded but never refused. Checking in again changes nothing.

distanceM.description: How far from the charger the position given on arrival was, in metres

nearCharger.description: Within 300 m of the charger; recorded, never enforced

post.description: The driver of an arrived booking starts charging: the charger is sent a remote start with the booking's idTag. The answer is the session: `starting` until the charger reports StartTransaction (then `charging`, pushed as `session:update`), or `failed` with a reason and copy to show, after which starting again retries. A charger that refuses because a stale transaction is open is soft-reset and the start retried once. Before the slot starts (the driver plugged in early), or with `startAt` in the future, the session is `scheduled` and the remote start is sent at the slot start (or `startAt`); waiting is never billed. Starting while a start is pending or a session runs returns it unchanged. 409 `payment-pending` until the booking is paid.

startAt.description: Start charging later, inside the slot (for a cheaper night rate). The driver plugs in now; the booked hours were paid upfront and waiting is never billed.

post.description: The driver stops charging: a running session is sent a remote stop and stays `charging` until the charger reports StopTransaction, when it becomes `stopped` and the booking `completed`. A start not yet begun is abandoned and a scheduled start cancelled. Stopping again, or with nothing running, returns the session unchanged. 503 when the charger does not answer (unplugging the cable also stops it).

get.description: Status, energy, power, time and cost so far (rounded up to 5 minutes at the hourly price, capped at the quote) and when the charger last reported, for the booking's driver or host. The same shape is pushed over /ws as `session:update`.

post.description: Creates the driver's Stripe customer on first use and a SetupIntent for an off-session card. The first card saved becomes the default.

get.description: Brand, last four digits and expiry only.

post.description: The card bookings use when they do not name one.

get.description: The tax details platform reporting needs. The TIN is masked to its last three characters and the date of birth is never returned.

put.description: Stores the legal identity and tax identification number that EU (DAC7) and UK platform reporting need, and marks the host's tax details complete: a listing cannot be published without them. The TIN is checked against its country's format (a PPSN with its check letter for Ireland; a 10-digit UTR or a National Insurance number for the UK). The TIN and date of birth are encrypted at rest. Replaces any earlier details.

tin.description: Tax identification number: a PPSN or tax reference for Ireland, a UTR or National Insurance number for the UK

companyNumber.description: Companies Registration Office number (IE) or Companies House number (UK)

tin.description: Tax identification number: a PPSN or tax reference for Ireland, a UTR or National Insurance number for the UK

get.description: For the driver or the host, once a paid booking has finished or its session has stopped (409 before). The driver paid the booked hours upfront; the receipt shows that price, any refunds, and the session as evidence of what the charger did: start and stop, kWh delivered (meter start to stop), meter readings and power samples. Nothing is billed by energy or by minutes used. The driver sees their card; the host sees the card fee passed on to them and what they keep.

post.description: The driver rates a completed booking from 1 to 5, with an optional comment, once. The host's listing shows the average.

The driver of a completed, cancelled or no-show booking disputes it (the charge, a fee, or the session), for support to look into. One open dispute per booking; 403 for the host, 404 for anyone else, 409 before the booking has finished or while a dispute is open.

The host stops the booking session charging on their charger now (RemoteStopTransaction). The session closes when the charger reports the stop; the booking was paid upfront and is not refunded automatically. 404 for another host's charger, 409 when nothing is charging or the charger rejects the stop, 503 when it does not answer.

Support refunds a paid booking in full or in part, for anything the automatic rules do not cover (a session that went partly wrong, a dispute). The host's share and the application fee are reversed in proportion. Never more than what is left to refund (422). Admins only (ADMIN_USER_IDS).

amountCents.description: What to refund; the rest of what was paid when omitted (a full refund)

post.description: Verified against the Stripe-Signature header and processed once per event id; a redelivered event is acknowledged without repeating its effects.
